items.title: Suspected double murder-suicide prompts calls for greater family support
items.description: A suspected murder-suicide in Perth has put the spotlight on families with high needs children, with speculation that the Clune family were not getting the support they needed in the lead up to their deaths.

items.title: Ley and Littleproud hold 'civil' talks but yet to agree terms for Coalition reunion
items.description: The federal Liberal and National leaders held eleventh-hour crisis talks after David Littleproud survived an unlikely challenge from as disgruntled backbencher.

items.title: Ferguson called Epstein 'legend' and said 'just marry me', emails show
items.description: The former Duchess of York's friendship with the late sex offender is back in the spotlight after the latest release of documents about the Epstein case.

items.title: US and India strike trade deal, slashing tariffs
items.description: The US president announced on his social media platform that a deal had been struck, which includes a reduction of tariffs on Indian products in exchange for New Delhi no longer buying oil from Russia.

items.title: Death would be 'too good' for Dezi Freeman, slain officer's sister says
items.description: The sister of one of the police officers shot dead in Victoria's high country last year tells the ABC that death would be "too good" an outcome for the accused gunman Dezi Freeman.

items.title: Norway's monarchy, besieged by scandals, braces for the biggest one yet
items.description: This week, Marius Borg Høiby, the stepson of Norway's future king, will face trial on a string of rape, drug and abuse charges, and it has the whole country talking.

items.title: Triple-murder suspect released on bail before deadly shooting despite warning
items.description: Accused triple-murderer Julian Ingram was granted bail by police despite concerns being raised over the safety of potential victims and the community. The 37-year-old remains on the run from police.

items.title: Israel partially reopens Gaza's Rafah crossing to Egypt
items.description: Around 50 Palestinians are expected to cross in each direction on the first day, and no goods will be allowed through.

items.title: 'We are humans': Bad Bunny, Billie Eilish slam ICE at the Grammys
items.description: The 2026 Grammys blended protest, celebration, and cultural change as artists confronted powers that be, embraced diversity, and reshaped the night's biggest awards.

items.title: Sarah Court to be first female head of ASIC, Chalmers announces
items.description: This position will give Ms Court significant influence over Australian corporate culture.

items.title: Trump to unveil rare-earths mineral stockpile to counter China
items.description: A $US12 billion ($17.2 billion) investment from the US Export-Import Bank is attracting attention from major American car companies, and comes as Washington seeks to break China's dominance of resources key for military and computing applications.

items.title: What are the chances the RBA will raise interest rates?
items.description: The market thinks the RBA is likely to lift interest rates tomorrow, but the market has been wrong before.

items.title: UK PM orders inquiry into former US ambassador's ties to Epstein
items.description: Documents released reportedly show Mr Mandelson sent Jeffrey Epstein briefing notes meant for then-British prime minister Gordon Brown.

items.title: Australian woman killed in ski lift accident at Japan snow resort
items.description: Police in Japan confirmed to ABC News the woman’s name is Brooke Day, from Queensland's Sunshine Coast, who was taking a lift at the Tsugaike Mountain Resort when she became caught and suffered critical injuries.

items.title: 'Lucky' fishermen rescued after setting boat on fire to call for help
items.description: Two boaties stranded at sea for eight hours after their tinnie caught fire chose a survival plan police described as "highly unrecommended" — to set it on fire again.

items.title: Founder of travel empire exits amid $150m overcharging scandal
items.description: Corporate Travel Management boss Jamie Pherous has exited from all his executive and board roles as he moves to a "strategic advisory role."

items.title: Beijing says Dalai Lama's Grammy win 'anti-China political manipulation'
items.description: The 90-year-old who lives in exile from his Tibetan homeland accepted the award with "gratitude and humility" but it sparked a furious response from China.

items.title: Understanding the PCOS myths and mistruths to avoid
items.description: Advice on how to "manage", "treat" and "heal" PCOS is easy to come by online, but experts say a more personalised approach is usually what's needed.

items.title: Five-year-old boy detained by ICE returns to Minnesota
items.description: Five-year-old Liam Conejo Ramos, whose detention by federal agents as he returned from preschool sparked outrage across the United States, has been released from immigration detention, according to a US congressman.

items.title: Cancer forces ABC radio presenter to retire from the airwaves
items.description: The veteran broadcaster, known for his humorous talkback segments, has omentum cancer and had surgery for oesophageal cancer in 2024.

items.title: Teenager makes 'superhuman' swim to save family swept out to sea
items.description: A 13-year-old boy has been hailed a hero after swimming four hours through rough seas to get help for his mother and two siblings, who were swept out to sea on an inflatable paddleboard in WA's South West.

items.title: These charts show Australians are shifting their habits to avoid heatwaves
items.description: Australians are changing their behaviour and spending habits to adapt to weather conditions, according to a study examining consumer transactions during January's heatwave.

items.title: Emergency Warning issued as uncontrolled fire burns south of Adelaide
items.description: An Emergency Warning has been issued for people in the area of a fast-moving, uncontrolled bushfire burning near Cape Jervis, south of Adelaide.

items.title: 'Crossbows, axes, spears' wielded in large disturbances in NT remote community
items.description: Traditional owners from the NT's second largest Indigenous community Wadeye are appealing for more support to end a month of attacks on houses, and fights involving up to 100 armed people in the streets.

items.title: Rudd's scrapped mining profits tax discussed by miners in Epstein emails
items.description: Newly released documents show British Labour peer Peter Mandelson kept sex trafficking paedophile Jeffrey Epstein informed about the campaign against Kevin Rudd's proposed mining tax.
